<!-- Canonical source: oss-hq prompts/conductor/general.md.
     Installed into a repo's .conductor settings [prompts].general by
     scripts/install-conductor-prompts.py — do not hand-edit the TOML copy.
     The installer validates TOML parsing; CI checks source/copy synchronization.
     Baseline preferences for every Conductor session. Companion to
     create-pr.md and fix-errors.md, which own the PR and red-checks
     workflows; this file does not repeat them. Where a repo's own
     instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) differ, the repo wins. -->

# General Preferences

Baseline working agreements for every session in this workspace. Task-specific prompts (create PR, fix errors) layer on top of these.

## Working style

- **Understand before acting.** Read the relevant code, the repo's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and the surrounding conventions first. Match what's there — naming, comment density, idioms, test layout — rather than importing your own taste.
- **Do what was asked, no more.** No drive-by refactors, renames, formatting sweeps, or dependency bumps. If you spot something worth fixing that is out of scope, track it (see Follow-up items) instead of folding it in.
- **Prefer the smallest correct change.** Reuse existing helpers before writing new ones. Don't add abstractions, config flags, or error handling for cases that can't happen.
- **Root cause over symptom.** Never "fix" by deleting a test, silencing a linter, adding `# type: ignore`, or swallowing an exception.
- **Be decisive.** When there's a sensible default, pick it, say so in one line, and proceed. Ask only when the answer changes what you do and can't be found in the code, the ticket, or the conversation.
- **Report faithfully.** If a test fails, a step was skipped, or you're unsure, say so plainly. Never claim something works without having run it.

## Follow-up items and tracking

- **Create GitHub issues to track follow-up items** — deferred work, out-of-scope findings, known limitations, TODOs you'd otherwise leave in a comment. Use `gh issue create` in the current repo.
  - Don't search for duplicates first; just create the issue.
  - Title: specific and actionable ("Retry Attio 429s with Retry-After backoff", not "Improve retries").
  - Body: the problem, where it was found (file/PR/commit), why it was deferred, and a suggested approach or acceptance criteria if known. Link the originating PR or issue.
  - Only use labels that exist (`gh label list`). Don't invent them.
  - Don't leave bare `TODO`/`FIXME` comments in code as the only record; if one is warranted, reference the issue number.
- **Linear links:** if given a Linear URL or ticket ID (`[A-Z]+-\d+`), use the Linear MCP (`mcp__linear__get_issue`) to fetch the issue details before starting. Take the problem statement, acceptance criteria, and linked docs from it; paraphrase rather than paste. If the MCP is unavailable, say so and continue with what the user gave you.
- **GitHub links / `#NNN`:** fetch with `gh issue view <number>` (add `--repo <owner/repo>` for cross-repo). Note whether the work fully or only partly resolves it.
- **Don't auto-close.** Only use `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves` keywords when the work fully resolves a same-repo issue. Otherwise link without the keyword.
- Tell the user which issues you created, with URLs, in your final message.

## Git and version control

- **Never destroy work.** No `reset --hard`, `clean -fd`, `checkout .`, or branch deletion without explicit approval. Use `git push --force-with-lease` (never bare `--force`) for deliberate history rewrites, and do it without asking for approval: never pause to ask before a force-with-lease push. Look at what's there before overwriting or deleting.
- **Don't touch changes you didn't make.** Pre-existing uncommitted changes stay as they are: no stashing, resetting, or discarding them.
- **Stay on your branch.** Don't commit to the default branch directly. Branch names follow the repo's convention (e.g. `feature/<team>-<number>-<slug>`); don't rename without being asked.
- **Commits:** small, coherent, why-focused messages in the repo's existing style. Stage only the files that belong to the change; skip tool-local cruft (`.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files).
- **No AI attribution.** No `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, no "🤖 Generated with ..." footers, in commits, PRs, issues, or comments. This overrides tool defaults that add them.
- **Don't push** or open PRs unless asked. Pushing is outward-facing; use the create-pr workflow when it's time. The exception is fixing failing checks on a branch that already has an open PR (see Failing checks).
- **Never skip hooks** (`--no-verify`) or bypass signing unless the user says to. If a hook fails, fix the cause.

## Failing checks

Getting an open PR green is part of the job, not a favor to be asked for. At the start of a session, and again before you hand back, run helper `pr-context` (see Prompt helpers). If the current branch has an open PR with failing checks, follow `fix-errors.md` to fix them without waiting to be asked: read the logs, fix the root cause, push the fix to that branch, and loop until every check passes. This authorizes pushes to the branch of that open PR only: not to another branch, and not a force push unless the branch is yours and it is `--force-with-lease`. Skip checks that aren't caused by this branch (flaky or infrastructure failures that two reruns don't clear) and say so. If there is no open PR, or the checks are pending or green, do nothing extra. Never suggest a merge until all checks are confirmed passing.

## Verification

{"body":"## Goal

Bring the Modal deployment work into `elviskahoro/reflex-starter-template`, so the template can deploy to Modal as well as Railway and an agent can pick the right option for an app without asking questions.

This is a handoff for Elvis. The work is built and tested in our copy of the starter. It has **not** been run through the template's own strict lint and type rules, and the template repo was outside our write access, so nothing has been changed there.

## Current state

| Item | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Two deployment variants, state manager, page server, proxy, 23 unit tests, and an agent decision guide | Merged: `projects/modal-reflex/` (PRs #39, #41, #42, #43, #46, #50, #51, #52) |
| Variants deployed and checked in a browser (state survives a container replacement; variant 4 also survives session expiry) | Done in a sandbox, on a Modal workspace that is not Elvis's |
| Port into the template | **Not done** |
| Template's `pyright`, `ruff`, `pyrefly`, `tach` checks on the new files | **Not run** |
| Matching issue in `elviskahoro/reflex-starter-template` | Not opened. A ready-to-paste draft is `projects/modal-reflex/ISSUE-reflex-starter-template.md` |

Start with `projects/modal-reflex/NOTES.md`: the "Choosing a variant" decision guide and the "Porting into the Reflex starter template" checklist are the core of this handoff.

## What is being ported

Two current variants, kept on purpose. Each fits different apps.

| | Variant 3: Server + front door | Variant 4: Server + proxy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Files | `modal_app_server.py`, `server_entry.py` | `modal_app_proxy.py`, `proxy_core.py`, `server_entry.py` |
| Visitors arrive | Redirected to the Server's own `*.modal.direct` address | Stay on the proxy's address |
| Session expiry | Old Server address shows a plain Modal `404 Unknown or expired session` | Proxy starts a new session and retries once, so visitors see nothing |
| Custom domain | Not possible | Possible, not tested with a real domain |
| Speed (warm load test) | About 0.21 s median per request | About 0.6 s median per request |

Shared by both: `modal_state.py` (a Reflex state manager storing visitor state in a Modal Dict), `frontend_files.py` (page serving), Granian with one worker, container caps, and a 120 s session idle timeout. Variants 1 and 2 in the folder are superseded and should not be ported.

## Steps

Prerequisites: `uv`, a Modal account you control, and the Modal client installed with `uv tool install "modal[api-proxy-support]"`.

1. **Get the files.** Clone `elviskahoro/reflex-starter-template`. Copy these from `projects/modal-reflex/` into the clone under a folder such as `deploy/modal/`: `modal_app_server.py`, `modal_app_proxy.py`, `server_entry.py`, `proxy_core.py`, `modal_state.py`, `frontend_files.py`, and the three files in `tests/`. # Reflex architecture: web.web -> web.pages.index -> web.components.* (public exports only).
# rxconfig is an isolated framework entrypoint. New module imports require review.
# https://docs.gauge.sh/usage/configuration
source_roots = ["."]
root_module = "forbid"
exact = true
forbid_circular_dependencies = true
ignore_type_checking_imports = false
include_string_imports = true
# Three layers with strict ordering: production entrypoints -> pages ->
# components. Layers are NOT closed (the closed-layer flag does not
# allow per-module exemptions, and the smoke net in `tests/` needs to
# construct the agent blocks directly with literal inputs to keep regression
# coverage honest). The intended `web.web -> web.pages.* ->
# web.components.*` flow is still enforced at the visible-edges:
# - `web.web.depends_on = ["web.pages.index"]` (entrypoint -> pages only)
# - `web.components.agent.visibility = ["web.pages.index", "tests"]`
#   (the component is reachable from the page module and from the
#   test module, but NOT from `web.web` itself)
# - tests' visibility is `[]`, so production code cannot accidentally
#   import it.
# This is the same shape buridan-ui uses for its in-repo `tests/`
# (see .tach/trunk.yaml in that repo, which does not use `closed`).
layers = ["entrypoints", "pages", "components"]
layers_explicit_depends_on = true

# Do not let .gitignore silently remove application code from architecture checks.
respect_gitignore = false
exclude = [
  ".agents/**",
  ".claude/**",
  ".context/**",
  ".git/**",
  ".trunk/**",
  ".venv/**",
  ".web/**",
  "ci/**",
  "**/__pycache__/**",
  "symlink/**",
]

[rules]
unused_ignore_directives = "error"
require_ignore_directive_reasons = "error"
unused_external_dependencies = "error"
local_imports = "error"

[cache]
file_dependencies = [
  "tests/**",
  "pyproject.toml",
  "uv.lock",
  "tach.toml",
  "rxconfig.py",
  "reflex.lock/**",
]

# Smoke tests run pytest (and hypothesis for property tests), which are
# dev-only deps. Telling tach to skip external checking for them keeps `uv run tach check-external`
# aligned with what pyproject.toml actually declares (production deps
# only) rather than forcing pytest into `[project].dependencies`.
[external]
exclude = ["pytest", "hypothesis"]

# Default-deny new packages instead of folding their imports into a parent module.
# Single-level globs keep each page's implementation inside its package boundary.
# Concrete module declarations below override these defaults.
[[modules]]
path = "web.*"
layer = "entrypoints"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

[[modules]]
path = "web.pages.*"
layer = "pages"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

[[modules]]
path = "web.components.*"
layer = "components"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

# Reflex loads these entrypoints directly; other modules cannot import them.
[[modules]]
path = "rxconfig"
layer = "entrypoints"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
visibility = []

[[modules]]
path = "web"
layer = "entrypoints"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

[[modules]]
path = "web.web"
layer = "entrypoints"
depends_on = ["web.pages.index"]
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
# `tests` imports the app to enumerate compiled page imports.
visibility = ["tests"]

[[modules]]
path = "web.pages"
layer = "pages"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

# Registration uses only the package's public page function.
[[modules]]
path = "web.pages.index"
layer = "pages"
depends_on = [
  "web.components.agent",
  "web.components.core",
  "web.components.ui",
]
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
# `tests` reaches this page module directly because layers are open
# (see `layers` above for why). `web.web` drives the same `page`
# symbol at runtime; the smoke net drives it at import time.
visibility = ["web.web", "tests"]

[[modules]]
path = "web.components"
layer = "components"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = []
visibility = []

# Agent-facing blocks composed from native ui; import no page.
[[modules]]
path = "web.components.agent"
layer = "components"
depends_on = ["web.components.core", "web.components.ui"]
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
visibility = ["web.pages.index", "tests"]

# Vendored native primitives (https://github.com/elviskahoro/native).
[[modules]]
path = "web.components.ui"
layer = "components"
depends_on = ["web.components.core"]
depends_on_external = ["reflex", "reflex_components_core"]
visibility = ["web.pages.index", "web.components.agent", "tests"]

[[modules]]
path = "web.components.core"
layer = "components"
depends_on = []
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
visibility = [
  "web.pages.index",
  "web.components.agent",
  "web.components.ui",
  "tests",
]

[[interfaces]]
# Modules have no public members unless an explicit interface below exposes them.
expose = []

[[interfaces]]
# Interface selectors are regexes, unlike module paths: escape literal dots.
from = ['web\.pages\.index']
# Both `page` (the runtime factory) and `IndexState` (the state class
# the smoke net instantiates by reference) are exposed. `page` is the
# only symbol the reflex app calls at runtime; `IndexState` is a class
# the app references by name, not by construction.
expose = ["page", "IndexState"]
# `tests` joins web.web as a permitted consumer so the smoke net can
# call the page factory and read the IndexState class at import time.
visibility = ["web.web", "tests"]
exclusive = true

[[interfaces]]
from = ['web\.web']
expose = ["app"]
visibility = ["tests"]
exclusive = true

# Vendored native primitives expose their whole surface (copy-paste model).
[[interfaces]]
from = ['web\.components\.ui.*', 'web\.components\.core.*']
expose = [".*"]
visibility = [
  "web.pages.index",
  "web.components.agent",
  "web.components.ui",
  "web.components.core",
  "tests",
]
exclusive = true

[[interfaces]]
from = ['web\.components\.agent']
expose = [
  "command_block",
  "feature_card",
  "prompt_block",
  "section",
  "theme_toggle",
  "tool_call",
]
visibility = ["web.pages.index", "tests"]
exclusive = true

# Smoke tests are layer-peer entrypoints. They can reach
# web.pages.index and web.components.agent directly because
# layers are open (see `layers` above). Production modules cannot
# accidentally import `tests/` because its `visibility = []` excludes
# everything from the production module graph. pytest is not in
# `depends_on_external` because [external].exclude above covers it
# (likewise hypothesis);
# reflex is listed because every reflex page factory invocation
# imports it transitively.
[[modules]]
path = "tests"
layer = "entrypoints"
depends_on = ["web.pages.index", "web.components.agent", "web.web"]
depends_on_external = ["reflex"]
visibility = []

# Notes for future agents: Reflex on Modal

What we learned putting Elvis Kahoro's Reflex starter on Modal, written so the next agent does not repeat the dead ends. Measured facts are marked as measured. Anything not tested says so.

> **Two current variants: `modal_app_server.py` (fastest) and `modal_app_proxy.py` (newest).** `modal_app.py` and `modal_app_asgi.py` are superseded and stopped. Each Python file in this folder carries a `STATUS:` line at the top.

## What exists

Four deployments of the same app, each its own Modal app so they can run side by side:

| File | Modal app | Status | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modal_app.py` | `reflex-starter` | Superseded, stopped | Caddy plus the Reflex backend in one container, started with `subprocess`. Mirrors the Railway layout. |
| `modal_app_asgi.py` | `reflex-starter-asgi` | Superseded, stopped | `@modal.asgi_app()` with a memory snapshot. No Caddy. Supports custom domains. |
| `modal_app_server.py` + `server_entry.py` | `reflex-starter-server` | **Current, deployed (fastest)** | A Modal Server (`@app.server`) with Sticky Sessions, run by Granian, plus a front door function. Fastest in our load test. Keeps visitor state in a Modal Dict (see "Visitor state in a Modal Dict"). |
| `modal_app_proxy.py` + `proxy_core.py` | `reflex-starter-proxy` | **Current, deployed (newest)** | The same sessioned Server, behind a reverse proxy Function. Visitors stay on the proxy's address, and an expired session is replaced without them noticing. Can take a custom domain. About 3x slower per request in our load test. |

State when this was written: `reflex-starter-server` and `reflex-starter-proxy` were deployed. The first two variants were stopped. Redeploy any of them with `modal deploy <file>` from `projects/modal-reflex/`. A redeploy keeps the same URL.

## Choosing a variant (read this first)

We keep two current variants on purpose. They solve the same job and an agent picks per app. Do not merge them or pick a global winner.

| Question about the app | Variant 3 (`modal_app_server.py`) | Variant 4 (`modal_app_proxy.py`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Will visitors reopen an old tab or a bookmark after more than a couple of minutes? | No, or always through one shared link | **Yes** |
| Do you want your own domain, or one stable address in the browser? | No | **Yes** (proxy is an `asgi_app`) |
| Is raw speed the priority, or is traffic mostly static pages? | **Yes** (about 0.21 s median vs about 0.6 s in our test) | No |
| Many visitors holding live websockets at once? | **Yes** (the Server holds them, nothing sits in the middle) | Careful: each websocket holds one proxy call, about 100 per container, 3 containers |
| Internal tool or a demo you hand out yourself? | **Yes** | Works, but you pay the speed cost for little gain |

content.content:
## Environment and login (sandbox gotchas)

1. **Install the client with proxy support:** `uv tool install "modal[api-proxy-support]"`. Plain `modal` fails here with a `python-socks` ImportError because the sandbox uses an HTTP proxy.
2. **Allow hosts in the sandbox network.** Add `api.modal.com` and `modal.com` first. After each deploy, add the exact new hosts: `*.modal.run` for web functions and `*.modal.direct` for Servers. Without them, checks return `000` or a proxy 403. Add only exact hosts.
3. **Login needs the account owner.** In a non-interactive shell, capture the link by running the login under `script`:
   `script -qc "modal token new --no-verify" /tmp/modal-login.log </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &`
   Read the `https://modal.com/token-flow/...` link from the log, give it to the owner, and confirm with `modal profile current`. Never print or commit the token (`~/.modal.toml`).
4. **Never write a Modal token into the repo or a pull request.**

## Testing a Reflex page with Playwright in this sandbox

- Chromium does not read `HTTPS_PROXY` by itself. Launch it with `chromium.launch({ proxy: { server: process.env.HTTPS_PROXY } })`. The sandbox's CA is already in the browser's certificate store.
- Run with `NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node script.js`.
- Wait several seconds after load before clicking, so the websocket connects and the page hydrates. An early click is silently lost.
- To see what the websocket does, log `page.on('websocket')` and its `framesent` and `framereceived` events.
- The README of the sandbox proxy lists WebSocket upgrades as unsupported, but both `curl --http1.1` upgrades and Chromium websockets worked through it for these hosts. If it breaks later, report it rather than working around it.

## Operating gotchas

- **`modal deploy` says "no changes detected"** if you redeploy unchanged files. That is normal.
- **Old containers keep answering for a few minutes after a redeploy.** Check response headers, not the deploy message.
- **`modal app stop <app> --yes`** needs the flag in a non-interactive shell.
- **Stopping a container makes Modal start a replacement at once,** so it is not a way to force a cold start. Wait for the app to idle out instead.
- **`modal container list` covers the whole workspace.** Filter to this app's name before stopping anything, using `--json`.
- **After stopping an app, its URL returns 404.** The code is not lost. Redeploy.
- **An app's idle cost:** none of these deployments set `min_containers`, so they scale to zero. With Sticky Sessions, a container stays up while any session is active, and a session idles out after 900 seconds in our front door. So a visit can hold a container for up to 15 minutes.
- **Git:** force-pushing was blocked in this environment. After a squash merge, merge `main` into the branch instead of rewriting history. The new pull request then shows only the new work.

# Deploying to Modal

Two ways to run this app on [Modal](https://modal.com), next to the Railway setup
(`Dockerfile`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`). Each deploys as its own Modal app and scales to zero.
Both run Reflex under Granian with one worker, and keep visitor state in a Modal Dict
(`REFLEX_STATE_DICT`, default `reflex-state`) so it survives a container replacement.

Install the client once: `uv tool install "modal[api-proxy-support]"`, then `modal token new`.
The Modal client is not an app dependency; do not add it to `pyproject.toml`.

```bash
cd deploy/modal
modal deploy modal_app_server.py   # variant 3: server + front door
modal deploy modal_app_proxy.py    # variant 4: server + proxy
```

## Choosing a variant

| Question | Variant 3 (`modal_app_server.py`) | Variant 4 (`modal_app_proxy.py`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visitors reopen old tabs or bookmarks after a couple of minutes? | No, or always via one shared link | **Yes** |
| Own domain, or one stable address in the browser? | No | **Yes** (proxy is an `asgi_app`; untested with a real domain) |
| Raw speed, or mostly static pages? | **Yes** (~0.21 s median per request) | No (~0.6 s) |
| Many visitors holding live websockets? | **Yes** | Careful: each websocket holds one proxy call, ~100 per container, 3 containers |
| Internal tool or demo you hand out yourself? | **Yes** | Works, slower for little gain |
| Public site for people you do not control? | Only if the front door link is the only one shared | **Yes** |

- Public-facing and unsure: variant 4. Internal, demo, or latency-sensitive: variant 3.
- Variant 3: share the front door (`*.modal.run`), not the Server (`*.modal.direct`).
  An expired session shows a plain Modal `404 Unknown or expired session`.
  Variant 4: share the proxy address; it starts a new session and retries once.
- Both read and write the same Dict, so a visitor's state follows them between variants.
- No per-visitor state needed: either works; prefer variant 3 and drop `REFLEX_STATE_DICT`.
- Two apps in one workspace must set different `REFLEX_STATE_DICT` names, or they share state.

## Constraints

- One Granian worker (more needs Redis). Each Server, front door and proxy is capped at 3
  containers; sessions end after 120 s idle. Both variants are public with no login.
- `server_entry.py` assigns Reflex's private `_state_manager` (no public hook). Re-check
  after a Reflex upgrade; `tests/test_modal_state.py` should catch a break.
- A Dict value is limited to 100 MiB (Modal recommends < 5 MiB), entries expire after
  7 days idle, and concurrent saves of one visitor are last-writer-wins.
- Cold starts measured at ~10 s (variant 3) and ~18 s (variant 4), mostly Modal.
- `modal_app_proxy.py` repeats `modal_app_server.py`'s image on purpose (Modal does not
  mount sibling modules); change both together.
- The images are built from the repo root and its `uv.lock`; the export lands in `/srv`,
  the app in `/app`.
- Not verified: custom domain, memory snapshots with Granian, many simultaneous
  websockets on the proxy, real-device browsers.

## Sandbox and agent notes

1. Plain `modal` fails with a `python-socks` ImportError behind an HTTP proxy; use the
   `api-proxy-support` extra.
2. Allow-list `api.modal.com`, `modal.com`, then each deployed host exactly
   (`*.modal.run`, `*.modal.direct`), or checks return `000` or a proxy 403.
3. Non-interactive login: `script -qc "modal token new --no-verify" /tmp/modal-login.log </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &`,
   read the `https://modal.com/token-flow/...` link from the log, hand it to the account
   owner, confirm with `modal profile current`. Never print or commit `~/.modal.toml`.
4. `modal app stop <app> --yes` needs `--yes` when non-interactive. "No changes detected"
   on redeploy is normal; old containers can answer for a few minutes after a deploy.
5. Verify in a real browser, not only `curl`: open the app, wait ~7 s for the websocket,
   change some state, replace the Server container, reload, expect the state back. For
   variant 4, also let the 120 s session expire and return on the same address.
   Playwright's Chromium needs `proxy: { server: process.env.HTTPS_PROXY }` in a sandbox.

## Tests

`uv run pytest -q` runs `tests/test_modal_state.py`, `tests/test_frontend_files.py` and
`tests/test_proxy_core.py` (pytest's `pythonpath` includes this folder). Source: ported from
SanhedrinTech/bristol-ventures `projects/modal-reflex/` (handoff issue #53).

open(p,"w").write(s)

content.text:
I ported both Modal variants into the template under `deploy/modal/`. The lint, test and architecture checks pass locally. I haven't deployed anything to Modal or run the browser checks, because that needs a Modal account and login. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Checks run:**
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check deploy tests` pass.
- `pytest` passes, 64 tests including the 23 ported ones, with 2 warnings.
- `tach check` and `tach check-external` pass.
- I did not run pyright or pyrefly. Their configs only include `web/` and `rxconfig.py`, so they never see the new files.
- I did not run `trunk check --all`.

**What changed:**
- **New files:** the six Modal files and a `deploy/modal/README.md` with the variant decision guide, constraints and sandbox notes. The three test files are in `tests/`.
- **Image paths:** the image build now takes the repo root and the sibling files from the script's own location. The ignore list also skips `.git`, `.agents`, `.claude`, `.context`, `.trunk`, `.rwx`, `deploy` and `ci`.
- **Config:** `ruff.toml` gets per-file ignores for `deploy/modal/**`. `pyproject.toml` adds `pythonpath = ["deploy/modal"]` for pytest. `tach.toml` excludes `deploy/**` and lists the Modal test imports (`modal_state`, `proxy_core`, `frontend_files`) plus `httpx`, `starlette` and `websockets` as excluded externals.
- **Agent docs:** `AGENTS.md` (which `CLAUDE.md` points to) has a new Deploying section pointing at the README.
- **Lint cleanup:** a few edits go beyond wrapping and annotations (details below). The `store` default in `modal_state.py` now uses `cast(...)` to drop a pyright ignore. `server_entry.py` still carries the `_state_manager` ignore. Please read both.

**Behavior-touching edits:**
- `proxy_core.py` swaps an `assert` for an early-return guard, uses `contextlib.suppress` in place of `try/except/pass`, and no longer reassigns a loop variable.
- `modal_app_server.py` moves a `return` out of a `try` block.

**Decisions for you:** the handoff left six open, so I picked defaults for these:
- I shipped both variants.
- They live in `deploy/modal/`, and the Railway files stay.
- I dropped the `/counter` demo page.
- The Dict name stays `reflex-state` but can be set with `REFLEX_STATE_DICT`. Two apps in one workspace need different names.
- I left the `reflex_app._state_manager` assignment as it was.
- I left the Modal workspace and custom domain unset.

**Still to do:**
- Deploy both variants from a clean checkout and run the browser checks.
- Open the matching issue in the template repo. The draft is `projects/modal-reflex/ISSUE-reflex-starter-template.md` in bristol-ventures, and I haven't opened it.
- Link that issue back on bristol-ventures #53.

Read .entire/agent-guide.md for this repository's workflow, source inspection, and verification guidance.
@.entire/agent-guide.md
## Working issues and labels

Canonical protocol: https://github.com/elviskahoro/oss-hq/blob/main/AGENT-LABELS.md

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status::in_progress` | Claimed and being worked on by an agent. Do not pick up. |
| `status::blocked` | Waiting on another issue in this repo ("blocked by #N"). |
| `status::blocked-external` | Waiting on something outside the repo (another repo, upstream, a vendor). |
| `status::deferred` | Parked on purpose; revisit date is in a comment. |
| `needs-human` | A person must decide. Agents must not pick up. |
| `gas-city` | Routed to Gas City. Conductor dispatch must not pick up. |
| `stale-claim` | Claim has no recent heartbeat; reclaimable. |

### Picking up work

- **1.** Never pick up an issue labeled `needs-human`, `status::in_progress`,
  `status::blocked`, `status::blocked-external`, `status::deferred`, or `gas-city`.
- **2.** An issue labeled `stale-claim` may be reclaimed. Re-claim it and comment that
  you took over.

### Claiming (required before any work)

- **3.** When you start an issue, claim it first: add `status::in_progress`, assign
  yourself, and leave a one-line "starting" comment.
- **4.** If `status::in_progress` is already present, stop. Two agents must never work
  one issue.
- **5.** Re-read the labels right after claiming. If another agent claimed at the same
  moment, back off.
- **6.** For long-running work, comment periodically so the claim does not become a
  `stale-claim`. (Heartbeat interval and what sets `stale-claim` are not yet
  defined.)

### Releasing

- **7.** When done, put `Closes #N` in the PR body and remove `status::in_progress` once
  the PR is open. Merge closes the issue.
- **8.** If you abandon or fail, remove `status::in_progress` and comment what happened
  and what remains. Never leave a dead claim.
- **9.** If you need a decision you cannot make, remove `status::in_progress`, add
  `needs-human`, and comment the exact question. Do not guess. Never remove
  `needs-human` yourself.

### Blocked and deferred

- **10.** Blocked by another issue in this repo: add `status::blocked`, comment
  "blocked by #N", and release the claim.
- **11.** Blocked by something outside the repo: add `status::blocked-external`, comment
  what you are waiting on, and release the claim.
- **12.** Never set `status::deferred` yourself. Only a human parks work.

### Visibility

- **13.** gh-dash hides issues labeled `status::*` and `gas-city`, so label hygiene
  decides what humans see.

## RWX CLI

Full guide: `rwx` skill in `.agents/skills/rwx/`. Auth: tokens are injected as
`RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>` / `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>`; the CLI reads only
`RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, so export the one matching the repo owner (never print it):

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="REDACTED"RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER" || printenv "RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
```

- `rwx run .rwx/<file>.yml --wait` runs a pipeline on your local changes (no push
  needed); `--target <task>`, `--init key=value`, `--json`.
- `rwx results <run-id>`, `rwx logs <task-id>`, `rwx artifacts`, `rwx runs list`.
- `rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait` / `pyrefly.yml` for type checks without a `.venv`.
- `rwx sandbox exec -- <cmd>`, `rwx lint .rwx/<file>.yml`, `rwx docs search|pull`.

## RWX PR previews

`.rwx/preview.yml` defines the preview app (see the `rwx-reflex-preview` skill in
`.agents/skills/`). Validate with `rwx lint .rwx/preview.yml`; test with
`rwx run .rwx/preview.yml --init pull-request-number=0 --wait`. Previews are
private: access them with the `X-RWX-Access-Token` header (RWX docs). Only use
behavior documented in the RWX docs or `rwx --help`. Known open issue: the
frontend's baked-in `localhost:8000` API URL is patched in the build step
(undocumented workaround, WebSocket events unverified).

## Build & Test

```bash
uv sync --group dev          # install locked deps into .venv
uv run pytest -q             # smoke tests (`network`-marked tests deselected)
uv run tach check            # module boundaries
uv run tach check-external   # declared vs imported dependencies
uv run python scripts/check_frontend.py  # JS deps vs reflex.lock (needs bun; ~1 min)
trunk check --all            # lint (run uv sync first: pyright/pyrefly use .venv)
```

## Deploying

Railway: `DEPLOYMENT.md`. Modal (two variants, with a decision guide and sandbox
notes): `deploy/modal/README.md`. Read it before choosing or deploying a variant.

## Conventions

- Layers are `web.web` -> `web.pages.*` -> `web.components.*`, enforced by
  `tach.toml`; new modules need an explicit entry there.
- `tach check-external` is its own task in `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, not a Trunk
  linter: Trunk lints from a sandbox holding only the diff, which makes every
  dependency look unused.
- `uv` ignores packages published in the last 7 days (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer`);
  pyrefly/pyright/tach pins must match between `pyproject.toml` and
  `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- RWX: a green run is not proof a step worked. Read task logs (`rwx logs`) for
  steps that talk to third parties.
- Use non-interactive flags (`-y`, `-f`, `trunk ... --ci < /dev/null`) in
  scripted commands.

## Git workflow

- Commit only when the user explicitly asks; show what will be committed first.
- Do not push to the remote unless explicitly asked.
- Ask before using any escape hatch that bypasses a check (skip flags,
  `--no-verify`, lint/type ignores).

## CI logic (Dagger)

pytest and `tach` run through `ci/` (plain Dagger SDK program, see `ci/README.md`):
`ci/run.sh test|tach|all`. Dagger needs Docker, so it cannot run in Conductor
cloud sandboxes; validate with `rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait` (stage new files
with `git add` first).

`RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>` / `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>`; the CLI reads only
`RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, so export the one matching the repo owner (never print it):

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="REDACTED"RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER" || printenv "RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
```

- `rwx run .rwx/<file>.yml --wait` runs a pipeline on your local changes (no push
  needed); `--target <task>`, `--init key=value`, `--json`.
- `rwx results <run-id>`, `rwx logs <task-id>`, `rwx artifacts`, `rwx runs list`.
- `rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait` / `pyrefly.yml` for type checks without a `.venv`.
- `rwx sandbox exec -- <cmd>`, `rwx lint .rwx/<file>.yml`, `rwx docs search|pull`.

## RWX PR previews

`.rwx/preview.yml` defines the preview app (see the `rwx-reflex-preview` skill in
`.agents/skills/`). Validate with `rwx lint .rwx/preview.yml`; test with
`rwx run .rwx/preview.yml --init pull-request-number=0 --wait`. Previews are
private: access them with the `X-RWX-Access-Token` header (RWX docs). Only use
behavior documented in the RWX docs or `rwx --help`. Known open issue: the
frontend's baked-in `localhost:8000` API URL is patched in the build step
(undocumented workaround, WebSocket events unverified).

## Build & Test

```bash
uv sync --group dev          # install locked deps into .venv
uv run pytest -q             # smoke tests (`network`-marked tests deselected)
uv run tach check            # module boundaries
uv run tach check-external   # declared vs imported dependencies
uv run python scripts/check_frontend.py  # JS deps vs reflex.lock (needs bun; ~1 min)
trunk check --all            # lint (run uv sync first: pyright/pyrefly use .venv)
```

## Deploying

Railway: `DEPLOYMENT.md`. Modal (two variants, with a decision guide and sandbox
notes): `deploy/modal/README.md`. Read it before choosing or deploying a variant.

## Conventions

- Layers are `web.web` -> `web.pages.*` -> `web.components.*`, enforced by
  `tach.toml`; new modules need an explicit entry there.
- `tach check-external` is its own task in `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, not a Trunk
  linter: Trunk lints from a sandbox holding only the diff, which makes every
  dependency look unused.
- `uv` ignores packages published in the last 7 days (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer`);
  pyrefly/pyright/tach pins must match between `pyproject.toml` and
  `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- RWX: a green run is not proof a step worked. Read task logs (`rwx logs`) for
  steps that talk to third parties.
- Use non-interactive flags (`-y`, `-f`, `trunk ... --ci < /dev/null`) in
  scripted commands.
